chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Sayf ibn 'Amira, from Suleyman ibn 'Amr, from Abu al-Maghra' al-Kassaf

He raised it, saying: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever mentions Allah, Exalted and Mighty, in private, has indeed mentioned Allah frequently. Indeed, the hypocrites used to mention Allah publicly and did not mention Him in private.'
They show off to people and do not mention Allah except for a little.

key_terms.يُراؤُنَ: They show off (to be seen by people)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between sincere dhikr and the dhikr of hypocrites?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates private dhikr as the true measure of sincerity, contrasting it with the hypocrisy of those who perform rituals for public acclaim while neglecting their inner connection with God. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on *ikhlas* (purity of intention), where the quality of one's devotion in solitude reflects the authenticity of their faith more than outward displays. It serves as a spiritual corrective to the tendency toward performative piety, reminding believers that God’s awareness of the unseen is the ultimate standard for acceptance.
